# Quick Start

Actor Mesh is a pub/sub bus, a runtime that forks a handler per tuple, and
handlers that are any process speaking stdio. The `ping-pong` example is a
complete two-actor mesh you can read end to end.

## Prerequisites

```sh
# Debian/Ubuntu
sudo apt install libnng-dev liblmdb-dev

# Fedora/RHEL
sudo dnf install nng-devel lmdb-devel gcc make
```

If your distro doesn't package nng, vendor it:

```sh
git submodule add https://github.com/nanomsg/nng.git vendor/nng
cd vendor/nng && mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make -j$(nproc)
# add -Ivendor/nng/include -Lvendor/nng/build to CFLAGS/LIBS
```

## Build

```sh
# Build the runtime (actor + proxy)
make
```

This produces:

```
bin/actor       — runtime binary
bin/mesh-proxy  — bus proxy
```

## Run the example

`examples/ping-pong/` is a two-actor pub/sub mesh: `pub.c` publishes a `ping`
tuple, `sub.c` subscribes to `pong`, and `ping-handler.sh` / `pong-handler.sh`
answer each topic. See `run.sh` for the full wiring (it compiles `pub` and
starts the proxy and two actors).

## Configuration

All behaviour is controlled by environment variables. See @appendix for the
complete reference. An actor is wired entirely from the environment:

```sh
ACTOR_ID=my-actor \
ACTOR_TOPIC=orders \
ACTOR_RESULT_TOPIC=orders_done \
ACTOR_HANDLER=./my-handler.sh \
ACTOR_LMDB_PATH=/tmp/my-actor \
ACTOR_BUS_SUB=tcp://127.0.0.1:5556 \
ACTOR_BUS_PUB=tcp://127.0.0.1:5557 \
./bin/actor &
```

## Stop

```sh
fuser -k 5556/tcp 5557/tcp   # free the bus ports
```

## Troubleshooting

**No response** — check that an actor is subscribed to your topic and publishing
a result, and that its `ACTOR_BUS_SUB` / `ACTOR_BUS_PUB` point at the proxy.

**"mdb_env_open: No such file or directory"** — the actor's LMDB directory does
not exist. Create the path in `ACTOR_LMDB_PATH` before starting the actor.

**Port already in use** — `fuser -k 5556/tcp 5557/tcp` or `pkill mesh-proxy`.
